title: Quantifying Protocol-Induced Uncertainty in Comparative Predictive-Model Evaluation: Evidence from Large-Scale Daily PM10 Forecasting
abstract: arXiv:2609.26288v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Comparative studies of predictive models often end by ranking candidate models, yet these rankings depend on evaluation protocols whose influence is rarely treated as a source of uncertainty. We formalize this problem as protocol-induced ranking uncertainty and introduce a framework that compares ranking displacement caused by switching protocols with displacement produced by conventional choices within a fixed protocol. We quantify these effects using the Protocol Sensitivity Score (PSS) and a full-refit intraprotocol reference.   We validate the framework in a large-scale sequential prediction study of daily PM10. Static-split and rolling-origin evaluation are compared across 425 European background stations and 365 US EPA monitors. Switching protocols produces mean PSS values of 0.801 and 0.772 and changes the selected model at 35.3% and 31.5% of stations, respectively. translated_title: 量化预测模型比较评估中协议诱导的不确定性：来自大规模日PM10预测的证据
translated_abstract: 预测模型的比较研究通常以对候选模型进行排名而告终，然而这些排名依赖于评估协议，而评估协议的影响很少被当作一种不确定性来源来对待。我们将这一问题形式化为“协议诱导的排名不确定性”，并引入一个框架，将切换协议所导致的排名位移与在固定协议内因常规选择而产生的位移进行比较。我们使用协议敏感度评分（PSS）以及基于完整重新拟合的协议内参考来量化这些影响。我们在一项大规模的日PM10序列预测研究中验证了该框架，在425个欧洲背景站点和365个美国EPA监测站上比较了静态分割评估与滚动起源评估。切换协议分别产生了0.801和0.772的平均PSS值，并分别在35.3%和31.5%的站点上改变了被选中的模型。在欧洲，具有相同评分目标的协议内扰动……
tldr: 该论文提出协议敏感度评分（PSS）框架，首次将评估协议的选择量化为模型排名不确定性的来源，并在大规模日PM10预测实验中发现，切换评估协议会在约三分之一的站点上改变最优模型的选择，其影响甚至超过协议内的常规扰动。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a Protocol Sensitivity Score (PSS) framework that formalizes evaluation-protocol choice as a source of ranking uncertainty, demonstrating in large-scale daily PM10 forecasting that switching protocols changes the selected model at roughly one-third of stations, exceeding the impact of conventional within-protocol perturbations.
